root_cause.text: The control message buffer was allocated with devm_kzalloc scoped to the USB device instead of the USB interface, so the memory was not freed when the driver was unbound (e.g., on probe deferral or configuration changes), causing a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `devm_kzalloc(&udev->dev, ...)` to `devm_kzalloc(&intf->dev, ...)`. The commit message states that USB drivers should tie device-managed resources to the interface to avoid memory leaks when drivers are unbound without device disconnection.

commit 9f2d3eae88d26c29d96e42983b755940d9169cd9
Author: Jakob Unterwurzacher <jakob.unterwurzacher@theobroma-systems.com>
Date:   Wed Apr 11 18:06:42 2018 +0200

    can: ucan: add driver for Theobroma Systems UCAN devices
    
    The UCAN driver supports the microcontroller-based USB/CAN
    adapters from Theobroma Systems. There are two form-factors
    that run essentially the same firmware:
    
    * Seal: standalone USB stick ( https://www.theobroma-systems.com/seal )
    
    * Mule: int
bic_trace_step.reason: In the `ucan_probe` function, the control message buffer is allocated with `devm_kzalloc(&udev->dev, ...)` (line ~740 in the full diff), tying its lifetime to the USB device (`udev`) instead of the USB interface (`intf`). This causes a memory leak when the driver is unbound from the interface (e.g., on probe deferral or configuration changes) because `devm_` resources scoped to the device are not freed on interface unbind. The fix requires using `&intf->dev` as the device argument. Since the commit introduces this allocation without proper scoping, the vulnerable construct is present and not fixed.
